Using the November 2021 Beige Book as context, the FOMC’s December 15 statement aligns with a cautiously optimistic outlook. District reports indicated economic activity picked up into October–November with stronger consumer spending and notable gains in leisure and hospitality, while supply chain disruptions and labor shortages continued to constrain output and weighed on light vehicle sales. Price pressures remained elevated. Against these mixed but improving fundamentals, the latest SLOOS showed banks broadly easing standards in residential real estate and consumer credit (including HELOCs and jumbos), raising card limits, and foreign banks easing CRE standards amid stronger demand; consumer credit demand strengthened and banks expect firmer C&I and credit card demand. This easier credit supply/firming demand backdrop supports continued gains in activity and employment and helps offset tapering headwinds, though Beige Book–flagged bottlenecks and labor tightness cap upside. Net: modestly more positive than prior, but still constrained.
